content.description: Illustration showing hands using a soft brush to clean the cylinder head

content.text: Using a soft brush and solvent, clean the head.
Do not clean the head in a hot tank as this will seriously damage it.

content.description: Illustration showing a precision straight edge and feeler gauge being used to check cylinder head flatness

content.text: (a) Using a precision straight edge and feeler gauge, check that neither the head nor manifold surface is warped.

content.description: Illustration showing measurement locations on cylinder head - four sides and diagonally across the head surface with arrows indicating measurement points

content.text: (b) Measure warpage at the four sides and diagonally as illustrated.

items: Maximum head surface warpage: 0.10 mm (0.0039 in.)
Maximum intake manifold surface warpage: 0.10 mm (0.0039 in.)
Maximum exhaust manifold surface warpage: 0.10 mm (0.0039 in.)
Maximum camshaft housing surface warpage: 0.10 mm (0.0039 in.)

content.text: If warpage is greater than specified value, replace the head.

content.description: Illustration showing use of dye penetrant to inspect cylinder head for cracks, with hand applying penetrant to head

content.text: Using a dye penetrant, check the combustion chamber, intake and exhaust ports, head surface and the top of the head for cracks.
If a crack is found, replace the head.

content.description: Illustration showing hands using a wire brush to clean valves

content.text: Use a gasket scraper to chip any carbon from the valve head.
Using a wire brush, clean the valve thoroughly.
